newsitem.title: DUBAI: "Largest" ancient Arabian tomb found in UAE.
newsitem.headline: "Largest" ancient Arabian tomb found in UAE.

text.p: Archaeologists in the Gulf Arab emirate of Ras al-Khaimah have discovered what they believe is the largest ancient tomb found in the Arabian peninsula, newspapers reported on Monday.
The circular tomb is said to be 4,300 years old and contemporary with the pyramids of Egypt. It would have stood about three metres (10 feet) tall and 14.3 metres (46.9 feet) in diameter, they said.
The tomb showed the ability of the area's ancient craftsmen to select and cut high-quality limestone blocks into a perfect circle, they added.

"It is difficult for modern masons equipped with 20th century machinery to achieve the results I have seen in this building," Derek Kennet, resident archaeologist at the emirate's national museum, was quoted as saying.
